transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm here because when I start eating, especially at night, I feel like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating anymore. It's really starting to scare me because I just can't seem to pull myself away once I start.
When these episodes occur, do you feel like you are consuming a significantly larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar period of time?

Yeah, it’s definitely way more than what normal people would eat, and I feel really embarrassed even admitting it. On bad nights when I'm stressed about school, I can go through two entire fast-food meals, a whole family-size bag of chips, and half a box of cereal in about an hour while sitting at my computer.
After these episodes of eating a large amount of food, do you ever feel the need to use methods like self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, or fasting to prevent weight gain?

I'm really ashamed to admit it, but at least a couple of nights a week I end up in the dorm bathroom forcing myself to throw up until my throat burns. I'll also chug water or take laxatives because I'm just terrified of all those calories showing up on the scale the next morning.
To clarify, do you engage in these purging behaviors or excessive exercise specifically following these episodes of eating large amounts of food?

Yes, I only do it right after those huge eating episodes because I panic about the weight gain. It's like a desperate attempt to "reset" everything and get the food out of me because I'm so terrified of what the scale will say the next morning. I don't do it at other times, just when I lose control like that.
